quotes.text: I would fast-track affordable and workforce housing, expand Accessory Dwelling Units, duplexes, and mid-rise housing in appropriate areas, regulate short-term rentals, tax vacant luxury and speculative properties, stop land banking, and require fair profit limits on public-backed projects.
quotes.editor_note: Verbatim, single sentence from Lucas-Tadeo's written Civil Beat 2026 Q&A on housing affordability — a campaign Q&A (text, not video-verifiable). States his build-more-locally, regulate-speculation approach (ADUs, duplexes, short-term-rental limits, vacant-property tax), a legible contrast with Green's build-more/deregulate framing. No edits.

quotes.text: Homelessness must be addressed by fixing the core issue, not just moving people around. Some people need mental health and addiction treatment; others fell on hard times and need housing, work and stability. I would expand emergency housing, connect people to care and create work-trade pathways in construction, agriculture, healthcare and public service so people can rebuild their lives and become self-sustaining.
quotes.editor_note: Verbatim from Lucas-Tadeo's written Civil Beat 2026 Q&A on his homelessness strategy — a campaign Q&A (text, not video-verifiable). States a treatment-plus-work-pathways approach, distinct from Green's service-expansion framing (kauhale villages, rapid re-housing). No edits.

quotes.text: I do not support liquefied natural gas as a long-term solution, but I would consider a temporary, limited transition only if Hawai'i's grid is not yet dependable and it lowers costs while replacing dirtier fuels. Any LNG use must have strict timelines, methane safeguards, and cannot delay renewable energy. Our real goal is energy independence through solar, battery storage, geothermal where appropriate and a reliable renewable grid.
quotes.editor_note: Verbatim from Lucas-Tadeo's written Civil Beat 2026 Q&A on the LNG-bridge question, which engages the same fossil-fuels-role axis as the Compass question but frames it locally. States a renewables-first, LNG-skeptical position with strict conditions, contrasting with Green's more LNG-embracing bridge-fuel stance. No edits.
